title: Dedicated staged rollouts: initial gate evaluator service (windowing + pause on missing metrics)
author: Logan Wright
body:
Context: Dedicated staged rollouts need a first-class gate evaluator that can continuously assess per-stage gates over time windows (latency, 5xx, queue depth, utilization, etc.) and safely pause when metrics are missing or late. This PR adds the initial implementation of the gate evaluator service + data model wiring in the control plane. It is intentionally conservative: evaluator never automatically advances stages; it only emits gate evaluations and can transition a rollout stage into HOLD when gates fail or metrics are missing. Related: ADR-027 (gate evaluation approach) and the broader rollout plan work in ENG-5121/5122/5123.

What’s included (v1): 1) New service: rollout-gate-evaluator (daemon) that runs an evaluation loop with jitter and per-pool concurrency limits; 2) Windowing semantics: per-gate EvaluationWindow support (duration, min_samples, allowed_lag, warmup) with sliding windows; evaluator queries [now-window, now] and applies aggregation per gate type; 3) Pause-on-missing-metrics behavior: if any required signal is missing/stale beyond allowed_lag, gate result becomes UNKNOWN and the stage is placed into HOLD with reason=MISSING_METRICS (fail-safe). For explicit FAIL results, stage is placed into HOLD with reason=GATE_FAILED. (Rollback automation is out of scope here; it will be in the stage controller / policy layer.) 4) Storage: writes GateEvaluation records to control-plane persistence (idempotent by rollout_id + stage_id + gate_id + window_end) and updates stage status summary (last_evaluated_at, last_result, hold_reason); 5) Metrics + logs: evaluator emits metrics for eval latency, query latency, missing-metrics holds, and per-gate result counts; includes structured logs with tenant_id/pool_id/rollout_id/stage_id/gate_id; 6) Guardrails: evaluator refuses to evaluate if rollout plan is not in an “active” state, ignores stage 0 shadow by default unless explicitly configured, and caps query fanout (max gates evaluated per tick) to protect the metrics backend.

Design notes: - We keep evaluator state minimal. The only "cursor" is the last successfully persisted evaluation window end per gate; if we miss ticks, we backfill up to a bounded lookback (default 10m) and then resume. - Missing metrics is treated as unsafe to proceed; this shows up as HOLD with a dedicated reason and a UI-visible message string (wired via stage status fields). - Query API is currently the TelemetryQueryClient abstraction (thin wrapper around our internal metrics service). Gate types implemented now: p95_latency_ms, error_rate_5xx, timeout_rate, queue_depth_p95, gpu_utilization_avg. - Cardinality: all queries are forced to aggregate to pool_id + stage_allocation_key only; tenant_id is included only as a filter (not a group-by). See comments in gate_queries.go.

Not included: - Automatic stage advancement; - Automatic rollback; - Quality-signal gates; - Multi-region sub-gates; - Customer-configurable query strings (we only support typed gates).

Rollout/ops: feature flag rollout.gates.evaluator.enabled (default off). In staging, enable with --enable-dedicated-rollouts-evaluator and set evaluator_tick=30s. On missing metrics, we currently HOLD immediately; no grace period beyond allowed_lag. SRE feedback requested on defaults.

Testing: - Unit tests for window calculation, idempotent persistence, and hold transitions; - Integration-style tests using FakeTelemetryQueryClient that simulates late/missing datapoints; - Load test not included; tracked in dedicated-rollout-load-test-plan.

Follow-ups: - Wire evaluator degraded mode -> global "hold" (ENG-512?); - Add sampling/backoff when metrics backend is degraded; - Add evaluation reasons to audit log emission in ENG-5128/PR-28558.

Screenshots: n/a (backend only).
commits: feat(rollouts): add rollout-gate-evaluator service skeleton + config
feat(rollouts): implement evaluation windows + backfill cursor
feat(rollouts): add typed gate queries for latency/errors/queue/util/utilization
feat(rollouts): persist GateEvaluation records + stage status summary updates
test(rollouts): fake telemetry client + missing-metrics/late-metrics scenarios
changed_files: services/rollout-gate-evaluator/** (new service, main loop, tick scheduler, concurrency)
controlplane/api/internal/rollouts/** (stage status summary fields for UI consumption)
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): The pause-on-missing-metrics behavior is what we want for Dedicated, but can we avoid flapping holds if the metrics backend blips for <1m? Right now allowed_lag default is 30s. Suggest default 2m and surface freshness in the hold reason.

Logan Wright (author): Agree. I bumped default allowed_lag to 120s for all default gates and added hold_message with last_datapoint_age_seconds so Console can show it. Keeping HOLD deterministic (no auto-resume) until we decide policy.
Jordan Lee (Policy): For idempotency, what happens if two evaluator instances are running (deploy overlap)? Any risk of duplicate writes racing and causing stage status to oscillate?

Logan Wright (author): Writes are idempotent on (rollout_id, stage_id, gate_id, window_end). Stage status update is conditional on plan_version + stage_generation and only moves "forward" in time; older window_end won’t overwrite newer summaries. Added a test for concurrent tick ordering.

Thomas Baird (Observability): Query fanout: we need a hard cap per tick per pool, and we should avoid grouping by tenant_id anywhere. Also please add a metric for query cardinality / series returned so we can watch for accidental explosions.

Logan Wright (author): Added max_gates_per_tick (default 50) and removed tenant_id group-by (filter only). Added telemetry_query_series_returned histogram and an alert TODO comment (dashboards PR will follow).
Allison Grant (Observability standards): Naming: prefer rollout_gate_evaluator_* for metrics. Also, emit gate_type label but NOT gate_id (too high cardinality).
Logan Wright (author): Updated metric names + labels. gate_id removed; gate_type retained. gate_id only in logs.
Ethan Park (Control plane): Please document the semantics of window_end: is it wall-clock now rounded to tick? This matters for UI and audit reasoning.

Logan Wright (author): Documented in evaluator README: window_end is tick_time truncated to 30s boundary (configurable), so we can reason about backfills. Also stored window_start/window_end explicitly in GateEvaluation.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Approved after defaults update. Please ensure missing metrics holds are noisy in logs with a stable code so oncall can grep quickly.
Logan Wright (author): Added reason_code=MISSING_METRICS / GATE_FAILED to logs and stage summary. Thanks.
release_notes: Internal: Adds initial rollout gate evaluator service for Dedicated staged rollouts. Evaluates typed gates over time windows and places stages on HOLD when gates fail or when required metrics are missing/stale (fail-safe). Feature-flagged off by default.
